leftEvidence.title: Mark preserves dazzling clothes and Peter’s fear

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: After six days Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain and is transfigured before them.
points.right: About eight days after the sayings Jesus takes Peter, John, and James up the mountain to pray; his face changes and his clothing flashes white.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Elijah and Moses appear speaking with Jesus; Peter proposes tents because he does not know what to say, a cloud overshadows them, and the voice commands listening.
points.right: Moses and Elijah speak of his departure to be completed at Jerusalem; sleepy disciples see glory, Peter proposes tents, a cloud brings fear, and the voice names the chosen Son.

payload.posture: Both preserve transformation, white clothing, Moses and Elijah, fearful witnesses, cloud, voice, and silence.

rightEvidence.title: Luke places prayer and an exodus conversation on the mountain

payload.tension: Luke adds prayer and the conversation’s subject; Mark states that Peter does not know what to say.
payload.title: Mark and Luke on the mountain
